title: Domain and Range: Ordered Pairs, Graphs, Rules and Interval Notation
seo_title: Algebra 1 Domain and Range Worksheets: Graphs, Functions and Interval Notation (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range.
meta_desc: Free Algebra 1 domain and range worksheets (F-IF.A.1, F-IF.B.5): ordered pairs, graphs with open and closed endpoints, linear, quadratic, absolute value and square root functions, interval notation and reasonable domains. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Domain = all the inputs (x). Range = all the outputs (y).
key_sub: Filled dot or ≤ means included: [ ]. Open dot or < means not included: ( ).
body_html:
How it works

The domain is the set of all inputs (x-values). The range is the set of all outputs (y-values). For a list of points, list each value once. For a graph, read the x-values from left to right (domain) and the y-values from bottom to top (range). A filled dot is included; an open dot is not.

Write intervals with inequalities (−2 ≤ x < 5) or interval notation ([−2, 5)): a square bracket means included, a parenthesis means not included, and ∞ always gets a parenthesis.

In a real situation, use a reasonable domain: you cannot buy −2 tickets or 2.5 tickets.

Example

Find the domain and range of {(2, 5), (−1, 3), (4, 5)}.

Inputs: 2, −1, 4.

Outputs: 5, 3, 5 (list 5 once).

Answer: Domain {−1, 2, 4}; range {3, 5}

Example

Find the range of f(x) = (x − 1)2 + 3.

The vertex is (1, 3) and the parabola opens up.

Answer: y ≥ 3

Example

Find the domain of g(x) = √(x − 2).

x − 2 ≥ 0.

Answer: x ≥ 2

Common mistakes

  • Swapping domain and range. Domain is x (inputs); range is y (outputs).
  • Listing a repeated value twice, or leaving a value out.
  • Using ≤ or [ for an open dot. Open dots mean the value is not included.
  • Giving “all real numbers” for something that must be a whole number or must be positive, such as tickets or time.

faq.q: What is the difference between domain and range?
faq.a: The domain is every input (x-value) a function can take. The range is every output (y-value) it gives.

faq.q: How do you find the domain and range from a graph?
faq.a: Read the x-values from the leftmost point to the rightmost point for the domain, and the y-values from the lowest to the highest point for the range.

faq.q: What is the range of a quadratic function?
faq.a: If the parabola opens up, the range is y ≥ the y-coordinate of the vertex. If it opens down, the range is y ≤ that value.
The inputs that make sense in the situation. A number of people must be a whole number, and time is usually 0 or more.

items.q: What is the range of g(x) = |x + 3| + 2?
items.e: An absolute value is never negative, so the smallest value of |x + 3| + 2 is 2. So y ≥ 2.

items.q: What is the range of h(x) = √(x − 4) + 4?
items.e: A square root is never negative, so the smallest output is 4: y ≥ 4.

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = −3x + 1?
items.e: A non-horizontal line goes up and down forever, so the range is all real numbers.

items.q: What is the range of g(x) = |x − 5| − 2?
items.e: An absolute value is never negative, so the smallest value of |x − 5| − 2 is −2. So y ≥ −2.

items.q: What is the range of g(x) = |x + 2| + 5?

items.q: What is the domain of h(x) = √(x + 4) − 5?

items.q: Movie tickets cost $11 each. C(n) = 11n is the cost of n tickets. A family can buy at most 6 tickets. What is a reasonable domain?
items.e: You can only buy whole numbers of tickets: {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}.

items.q: Movie tickets cost $11 each. C(n) = 11n is the cost of n tickets, and a family buys at most 6. What is the range?
items.e: Multiply each input by 11: {0, 11, 22, 33, 44, 55, 66}.

items.q: A ball is dropped from a 64 ft tower and hits the ground after 2 seconds. h(t) is its height. What is a reasonable domain?
items.e: Time runs from the drop (0 s) until it lands (2 s): 0 ≤ t ≤ 2.

items.q: A ball is dropped from a 64 ft tower and lands after 2 seconds. h(t) is its height in feet. What is the range?
items.e: The height goes from 64 ft down to 0 ft: 0 ≤ h ≤ 64.

items.q: A car's 15-gallon tank is full. It uses 1 gallon every 30 miles. G(d) is the fuel left after d miles. What is a reasonable domain?
items.e: The tank lasts 15 × 30 = 450 miles: 0 ≤ d ≤ 450.

items.q: A(w) = w(20 − w) is the area of a rectangle with perimeter 40 cm and width w. What is a reasonable domain?
items.e: Both the width and the length 20 − w must be positive: 0 < w < 20.

items.q: Which situation has a domain of whole numbers only?
c: The distance a car travels in t hours
The weight of p pounds of apples
items.e: You can't buy part of a pencil: the cost of buying n pencils.

items.q: Is the relation {(1, 4), (2, 5), (1, 6)} a function?
c: No, the outputs are not in order
No, the input 1 has two outputs
items.e: A function gives each input exactly one output. Input 1 gives 4 and 6: not a function.

items.q: What is the domain of f(x) = x2 − 3?
items.e: You can square any number: all real numbers. (The range is y ≥ −3.)

A gym membership costs $35 a month. C(m) = 35m is the cost for m months, for up to one year. What is the range?
items.e: Months are whole numbers from 1 to 12, so costs are multiples of 35 up to 420: {35, 70, …, 420}.

items.q: A phone battery drains from 100% to 0% in 20 hours. B(t) is the charge after t hours. What is the range?
items.e: The charge goes from 100 down to 0: 0 ≤ B ≤ 100.

items.q: What is the domain of the relation shown by the table: x = 2, 4, 6, 8 and y = 5, 9, 13, 17?
items.e: Only these four inputs are shown: {2, 4, 6, 8}.

items.q: Which interval is the domain of a function that is defined for every number greater than −3?
items.e: Greater than −3, not including −3: (−3, ∞).

items.q: Which set of points is a function with domain {1, 2, 3}?

items.q: A store sells boxes of 12 donuts. D(b) = 12b is the number of donuts in b boxes. Which number cannot be in the range?
items.e: Outputs are multiples of 12. 30 is not.

items.q: What are the domain and range of f(x) = 7 (a horizontal line)?
items.e: Every input is allowed, but the only output is 7: domain all real numbers, range {7}.
